title: Opta in Focus: Data and Analysis at the Start of the Premier League
seoTitle: Opta in Focus: Data & Analysis at Premier League Start
subtitle: With the season kickoff, the relevance of statistical analysis to understand club and player performance is highlighted.
excerpt: The Premier League kickoff underscored the importance of data analysis in football, with Opta mentioned in discussions about team performance and milestones.
author: Daniele Morais
sourceName: The Transfer Flow, The New York Times
contentHtml:
With the Premier League kickoff, the football world turns its eyes to in‑depth analyses of club and player performance. In this climate of intense debate and predictions, Opta, a name recognised in sports data analytics, emerges as a central point in conversations about the upcoming season.

The role of Opta in football analysis

Opta stands out for providing data that underpins detailed football analyses. Its presence is noted in discussions ranging from overall team performance to specific coaching milestones. For example, a source indicates that, according to Opta, a win would see Mikel Arteta become the fifth Premier League manager to reach 150 victories in fewer than 250 games.

In addition, Opta Analyst, an associated platform, contributes assessments of the transfer market. Ali Tweedale of Opta Analyst, for instance, outlined the extreme risk perceived in Tottenham’s signing of Savinho.

Performance analyses and expectations in the Premier League

The start of the Premier League is marked by expectations and evaluations of clubs’ futures. Sunderland, which surprised by finishing seventh last season and qualifying for Europe, is one of the teams under scrutiny. Despite that success, the side recorded an expected‑goals (xG) differential of –0.36 per 90 minutes last season, a figure worse than that of relegated West Ham and any other team that avoided the drop.

Ipswich Town, back in the Premier League, is also being watched closely. The club invested in signings, including goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen, who stands 2.06 m tall, whose save numbers were highlighted last season in USG. The Ipswich‑vs‑Sunderland match in the opening round is seen as a crucial showdown for both clubs in the battle to avoid relegation.

The transfer market and its implications

Transfer‑market activity is a decisive factor for team performance. Ipswich Town made signings regarded as shrewd, while Sunderland has been passive, with only one acquisition: 35‑year‑old full‑back Thomas Meunier on a free transfer. This suggests a heavy reliance on internal player development, such as striker Brian Brobbey.

Other promoted sides, like Coventry City and Hull City, are also under analysis. Coventry kept its champion‑core squad, and Hull’s deals appear sensible. However, with clubs such as Tottenham and Forest under‑performing, staying in the top tier will be a tough battle for the newly‑promoted teams.

Player highlights and strategies

Specific player analysis also gains prominence. Cole Palmer, for example, is identified as a player with high recovery potential under Xabi Alonso, especially considering his output when fully fit last season and his role in penalties, free‑kicks and corners. He is seen as a bet to outscore Bruno Fernandes in Fantasy Premier League points.

Conversely, Bruno Fernandes, despite being in several squads, is expected to regress. Erling Haaland, priced at £15.5 million, is questioned on whether the investment is justified given Manchester City’s midfield uncertainty and manager Enzo Maresca, even though he could still contest the Golden Boot in what is considered a weak season.

With information from The Transfer Flow, The New York Times.
